passage1.text: As a university student,I've come to realise just how little I know about money.I've come to the brutal realisation that Australia's youth are being done a great disservice by not receiving any consistent financial education. Diving headfirst into the crash course of starting university,I've quickly tried to get myselfup to speed with the financial terms ofthe modern era to help manage my personal finances. I've read some financial education books,done some online learning,and have spoken to my nearest and dearest for their pearls of financial wisdom. There are undoubtedly hundreds of great resources out there for those wishing to improve their financial literacy,but while I was researching,I still kept wishing that I didn't have to play catch-up with the money world.I felt that I was sailing the financial seas with no skills and no lifejacket! However,after talking to my friends who felt the same,I quickly realised that it wasn't my ignorance but the lack of financial education in our schooling system that is leaving high schoolers seriously behind in the modern world ofmoney. Let's compare a theoretical financial education subject to the standard compulsory English class.On average,English may not be the most popular subject,but it's consistently on the schedule throughout high school,with all students graduating fluent in English. A financial education subject should do just the same.It shouldn't be just a one-day event but a course integrated throughout the whole of high school that would allow students to gradually expand their financial literacy,and would prevent the need for a 'catch up'phase once we're out on our own after graduation In the same way that learning a language or new skills takes time,building financial skills requires practice and years to gradually accumulate bits and pieces ofknowledge. Giving young people the opportunity to become familiar with the world ofmoney would provide them with a great advantage to enter adulthood with confidence and security so that they are able to manage their own money and look after themselves.

passage2.text: Chocolates save us from many things,especially emotional distress.They comfort us in times of trouble, calming down a racing heart by channelling happy calories inside us.We all have faith in chocolates to delight us in an instant! Recently,chocolate lovers were heartbroken as scientists claimed that they can become extinct by 2050! But hey,we have some happy news for you.Scientists can still help save chocolates from dying out!If you are not aware as to why scientists made the statement about the death of this wonderful thing,let us tell you the facts.Chocolate trees,whose seeds are used to make chocolate,grow in the tropical plant world and require very specific weather conditions to prosper. Now,fifty percent of the world's cocoa(可可)beans come from two countries in West Africa:Cote d'lvoire and Ghana.Scientists believe that both of these countries will experience a 3.8°F temperature increase by 2050 due to global warming,endangering the cacao( 可 可 树 )farms in the rainforests.These farms will then have to be shifted to cooler mountainous areas,which are the natural habitat of wildlife.This will lead to some tough decisions:whether to grow chocolate or save wildlife. Unfortunately,the crisis of global warming has already had a serious negative impact on cacao farms' yields,leading to the prices of chocolates skyrocketing. Scientists,however,are trying to find a long-term and eco-friendly solution to this problem!They are trying to modify the species with a gene-editing technology,which will transform the seedlings into a species that survives even in a drier and warmer climate. According to a report by The Business Insider,in the University of California's new bio-sciences building,tiny green cacao seedlings are lined up in refrigerated greenhouses for a new experiment by using a technology called CRISPR.By manipulating the DNA of plants,this technology is already being used across the world to make plants tougher and cheaper.Similarly,in this unconventional experiment,scientists will make tiny,precise changes to the DNA of the seedlings to make the cocoa crops survive in warmer and drier climates.

paragraphs.A: For all the innovation and choice that define the food and drink industries,if you want to make money,you could do a lot worse than fill a bottle with water and sell it.A litre of tap water,the stuff we have cleverly piped into our homes,costs less than half a penny.A litre of bottled water can cost well over a pound, especially for something fancy that has been sucked through a mountain.
paragraphs.B: Yet the bottled water market is livelier than ever.It defies our increasing awareness of the harm plastics do to the environment and a broader,growing sense that something has to change.Sales in the UK were worth a record f558.4 million this past year,an increase of 7%,according to the latest figures from the market analyst Kantar.Separate data from other analysts show that last year the British consumed more than 2.2 billion litres of bottled water,including "take-home"and "on-the-go"products.That's an annual rise in volume of 8.5%.
paragraphs.C: Environmental campaigners are struggling to understand why nations blessed with clean tap water grow only fonder of the bottle."It's very surprising to me,"says Sam Chetan-Walsh,a political adviser at Greenpeace and campaigner against ocean plastic.“Public awareness has never been higher,but the message is not quite reaching all the people it needs to."Where it is heard,the message is causing concern.Plastic water bottles require oceans of fossil fuels to make and ship.Additionally,single-use plastics of all types are polluting our cities and seas.Numerous documentaries have shown how plastic is ultimately killing wildlife.
paragraphs.D: Moves against various plastics have gathered pace,from shopping bags to straws and plastic-lined coffee cups.Chetan-Walsh argues that bottled water is different because the alternatives are so obvious."Ifa product that is so nakedly unnecessary can exist,then the whole system is failing,"he says.
paragraphs.E: Hope is not entirely out of reach.The rate of growth has begun to ease (sales were up 7%in the year, compared with 8%the previous year).
paragraphs.F: But even if large numbers ofpeople are quitting bottled water because of care for the environment,others are taking it up.The introduction of the"sugar tax"on juices and soda drinks has pushed more people to bottled water,while health awareness has boosted its desirability.Tap water consumption is growing at roughly the same pace(UK consumers still drink almost three times as much tap water as bottled water).
paragraphs.G: So the plastic tide only creeps higher.The industry is quick to point out that all its bottles are recyclable. “But collection rates are,at the most generous estimates,56%,so the actual recycling rate will be lower than that,"Chetan-Walsh says.And while bottles may be recyclable,very few are made of recycled plastic.One water bottle company launched recycled half-litre "eco"bottles alongside its standard bottles.Another has pledged to use only recycled plastic across its range by 2025.Chetan-Walsh believes in a ban on single-use bottles.Bans do exist in some places.Organisers of a famous music festival announced that water bottles will not be sold this summer.San Francisco has banned them from city property and events.Last year,the UK government set out plans to ban single-use plastic from its estate.
paragraphs.H: Water bottlers,unsurprisingly,don't support bans.But they raise concerns about health rather than profit margins.Last month one chief executive of a water botling company said that bans would "result in greater consumption of sugary drinks,adding to all the health dangers of obesity,diabetes and tooth decay".Kinvara Carey,general manager of an association of the biggest bottled water manufacturers,cites a survey in which people were asked what they would do if bottled water were not available."Forty-four per cent would buy another drink,which is not great,14%would go without and 4.5%said they would find a fountain,"she says. “The choice is important.” D)What if fountains were more numerous,and tap water more clearly available in cafes,restaurants and elsewhere?Dozens of fountains are being installed in London.There are similar initiatives elsewhere.Before plastic and the marketing that made people think they needed bottled water in the first place,fountains were an urban fixture.Greenpeace,among others,is also pushing for a"deposit return"scheme.This would mean tax on bottled water would be refunded to customers who returned the plastic for recycling. J)Even if bottled water sales are growing slightly more slowly,the industry is racing to adapt to changing concerns and tastes.Flavoured water is booming:sales of the sparkling variety shot up by 20%,according to the latest analyst data.Meanwhile,international water brands,as well as a range of new companies,are selling high-end reusable bottles.And ifyou must fill them with tap water,why not add flavouring? K)As the owner of multiple sugary drink brands and bottled water,PepsiCo is facing challenges on health and environmental fronts.Last year,the company bought SodaStream(a drinks company that sells machines for making tap water bubbly and then consumers add flavours)for $3.2 billion.It also launched a range of fancy bottles that work with tap water and flavour packets.The bottle is reusable.The packets?Not so much,and, yes,they are made ofplastic,although the company invites users to post them back for recycling L)As is so often the case,clever marketing can beat reason;awareness is rarely enough.“There is always this kind of slip between concern,intent and changed behaviour,"says Giles Quick,an analyst of bottled water. “The best example is five a day,the recommendation to have at least five portions of fruit and vegetables every day.Almost everyone is aware of this,but something like 15%of us achieve it."Unless a far- reaching bottle ban does come into force,it will be up to consumers to not only demand change—but to act themselves.

questions.script:
Across the U.S., families are looking to the winter with fear as energy costs soar. A number of factors
are creating a bad situation: Global energy consumption is up, but supplies have been reduced. [1] The Energy
Department projects heating bills will jump 28% this winter for those who rely on natural gas. Natural gas is used by
nearly half of U.S. households for heat. Heating oil is projected to be 27% higher and electricity 10% higher. That
comes against inflation rates that accelerated last month with consumer prices growing 6.6%. That's the fastest
pace in four decades.
The pain will be especially acute in parts of the country that heavily rely on heating oil to keep homes warm.
It's projected to cost more than $2,300 to heat a typical home with heating oil this winter. [2] Last month, the federal
government added $1 billion in funding to Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program, bringing the total to $4.8
billion. But that represents a reduction from last year's energy assistance package of over $8 billion.

That's the main finding of a new study by researchers at the U.s. Department of Agriculture in Stoneville, Mississippi.
The study aimed to identify disconnects between how healthily Americans think they eat and how they actually
do. For the study, the researchers asked participants to rate their diet as excellent, very good, good, fair or poor. Folks

questions.script:
M: I need to stop at the bank to withdraw some cash.
W: Why not just pay with your phone?
M: Well, actually, I've stopped using online payments for the past three months now.
W: Stopped paying online? Oh, you must be worried that online payments aren't secure.
M: No, they are safe. [8] But paying online is too convenient and I spent too much money on things I didn't need.
W: [9] Oh, impulse purchases can be an issue for me, too. I've definitely bought clothes and shoes I didn't need
because they were on sale, and paying with my phone was so easy. But I've found that if I review my spending
every night, that keeps me from spending too much.
M: I tried that strategy, but it just didn't work, because I'd be busy studying all day. Then, when I was tired and hungry,
I'd use my phone to order food, like burgers and other junk, [10] instead of going to the canteen, where I could get
a healthier meal for half the price.
W: Well, what do you do now then? It seems like you'd have the same problems with cash.
M: I go to the bank once a week, and the rest of the time I keep my bank card at home, so I can't get more cash out.
And I also have a notebook where I record my expenses.
W: But what prevents you from just going to the bank and getting more money, if you want to buy something?
M: The first month I did withdraw extra cash twice, but I felt guilty about it. [ii] And after that I refused to spend
more than what I had budgeted, and by now it's just a habit.

questions.script:
[l6] Lift-off is usually the most environmentally harmful stage of any space mission, with vast quantities of fuel
burnt up in a matter of minutes.For instance, SpaceX's Falcon 9 gets through 112 tonnes of refined fuel, emitting about
336 tonnes of CO2. This is the equivalent produced by your average car driving almost 70 times around the world. [16]
As well as greenhouse gases, rocket engines emit particles that destroy ozone. These issues are growing more pressing
with the emergence of commercial spaceflight. There were 114 space launches in 2020, but there may be up to 1,000
per year in future.
Sustainable fuels are the top priority to enable greener space travel. Current spacecraft use a variety of fuels, but
most are based on fossil fuels. One potentially greener option is liquid hydrogen and oxygen. Hydrogen can be obtained
sustainably by using solar power to break water down into oxygen and hydrogen.
Reusable rockets can cut down on some of the waste associated with spaceflight. [17] Traditionally, boosters, fuel
tanks and other components are treated as expendable. But guiding them back to Earth in a controlled manner opens
new possibilities—most components from the Falcon 9 can be reused up to 100 times.
Truly environmentally friendly space travel is still some way off. [18] But we already have many of the technologies needed to start limiting its impact on our planet.

questions.script:
Helping to look after a pet can facilitate numerous aspects of a child's emotional development. [19] Research
shows that reading to a loyal and nonjudgmental companion, such as a dog or cat, can encourage reluctant readers to
read aloud, which will in turn boost their self-confidence. Having a companion to talk to about their feelings can also
help children feel secure and develop communication skills.
A household pet can also cultivate a child's sense of responsibility as their parent explains the necessary processes
of keeping their pet happy and healthy. As a child matures, they can then take on more of the daily responsibilities,
boosting their sense of independence.
[20] Pets also provide a fantastic subject for research and learning. Parents can encourage their child to research
their favourite pets at the library or during a supervised internet search. Taking children along to the pet shop to buy
food and supplies will support their cognitive development as their passion for learning flourishes.
A child's physical development can benefit greatly from taking pets for walks in the fresh air. Even their fine-
motor skills can be utilised in taking care of a beloved animal.
When responsibilities are well paced and communicated, a child can benefit greatly from involvement in bringing
up a happy and healthy pet. [2i] And of course, if a child doesn't have a pet in their own household, they can still
benefit from all of the above when visiting a friend who does.

students a packet of information. This would include costs of college, grants and scholarships. It would also include
expected monthly loan payments and projected salary after college.
State Representative Adam Mathews is one of the two legislators who proposed the bill. He said it would give
prospective students more information about what to expect once they graduate."Putting that information in front of
them will give them the best opportunity to match their skills and their dreams to what our schools can provide, said
Mathews. [23] He notes that the state can only regulate public institutions in this way, but he hopes private institutions
in Ohio follow the lead of the state and post similar information. He believes giving out this information will help

their very reasonable cost.

colleges out of state. [25] Many colleges and universities currently provide similar information on their websites.

require the universities and colleges to send a packet directly to students.

questions.expl: 短文明确提到“Ohio's schools are already competitive”，即“颇具竞争力”。选项A“资源丰富”、C“提供实现梦想的最佳机会”、D“对其他州学生最具吸引力”均未提及，原文仅说“吸引的本科生比送往外州的多”。 涉及知识点：听力短文事实细节直接定位

options.A: Some students waste much time surfing the net.
options.B: Students may need to visit too many websites.
options.C: Students have to search for the information.
options.D: Some students may lack adequate access. Part Ⅲ Reading Comprehension (40 minutes)

questions.script:
[22] A new bill in the Ohio legislature would require state public colleges and universities to send prospective
students a packet of information. This would include costs of college, grants and scholarships. It would also include
expected monthly loan payments and projected salary after college.
State Representative Adam Mathews is one of the two legislators who proposed the bill. He said it would give
prospective students more information about what to expect once they graduate."Putting that information in front of
them will give them the best opportunity to match their skills and their dreams to what our schools can provide, said
Mathews. [23] He notes that the state can only regulate public institutions in this way, but he hopes private institutions
in Ohio follow the lead of the state and post similar information. He believes giving out this information will help
Ohio's colleges and universities to be more competitive. The information will highlight what a great value they have for
their very reasonable cost.
[24] Ohio's schools are already competitive. The state attracts more undergraduate students than it sends to
colleges out of state. [25] Many colleges and universities currently provide similar information on their websites.
This includes tuition, fees, graduation rates and more, But students need to search for the information. This bill would
require the universities and colleges to send a packet directly to students.
questions.expl: 原文提到“Many colleges and universities currently provide similar information on their websites... But students need to search for the information”，即问题是“学生必须自行查找信息”。选项A“浪费时间上网”、B“访问太多网站”、D“缺乏访问权限”均未提及。 涉及知识点：听力短文转折关系捕捉（but 引出问题核心）、同义替换（have to search for the information 对应 need to search for the information）

questions.stem: 第 26 空
questions.expl: ) revealed 详解：语法判断：空格前为主语“new research”，后为that宾语从句，需填动词过去式作谓语。语义判断：句子阐述研究成果，“revealed”（揭示、显示）符合语境，指新研究揭示了视力剥夺对脑细胞的影响。 涉及知识点：动词时态（一般过去时）、语义搭配（research 与 reveal 搭配表“研究揭示”）

questions.stem: 第 27 空
questions.expl: ) interact 详解：语法判断：空格位于定语从句中，主语“brain cells”，后接“with one another”，需填动词原形与with搭配。语义判断：“interact with”（与……相互作用）符合语境，指视力剥夺改变脑细胞间的相互作用方式。 涉及知识点：动词固定搭配（interact with）、一般现在时（描述普遍现象）

questions.stem: 第 28 空
questions.expl: 详解：语法判断：主语“This study”，后为what宾语从句，需填动词第三人称单数作谓语。语义判断：引用研究作者的话，强调研究对已有认知的“强化”作用，“reinforces”（加强、强化）符合语境。 涉及知识点：动词第三人称单数（一般现在时）、语义逻辑（研究成果与已有认知的关系）

questions.stem: 第 29 空
questions.expl: 详解：语法判断：空格前为“a”，后为“effect”，需填形容词作定语。语义判断：前文提到视力剥夺能增加神经元灵敏度，此处指“显著影响”，“significant”（显著的）符合语境，“have a significant effect on”为固定搭配。 涉及知识点：形容词修饰名词（significant effect）、固定短语（have an effect on）

questions.stem: 第 30 空
questions.expl: ) closed 详解：语法判断：空格前为“have”，需填过去分词构成不定式完成式（to have done）。语义判断：结合“auditory learning window”（听觉学习窗口），“closed”（关闭）符合语境，指传统认为该窗口关闭后听觉能力不再变化。 涉及知识点：不定式完成式（to have + 过去分词）、语义逻辑（窗口关闭与能力变化的关系）

questions.stem: 第 31 空
questions.expl: ) adaptable 详解：语法判断：空格前为“were not”，需填形容词作表语。语义判断：后文提到卡诺德的研究推翻了传统观点，传统观点认为童年关键期后大脑感觉区域不再“具有适应性”，“adaptable”（能适应的）符合语境。 涉及知识点：形容词作表语、语义对比（传统观点与研究结论的矛盾）

questions.stem: 第 32 空
questions.expl: ) readily 详解：语法判断：空格前为“learn languages much more”，后为“than adults”，需填副词修饰learn。语义判断：“readily”（快速地、轻而易举地）符合语境，指儿童比成人学习语言更快速。 涉及知识点：副词修饰动词（readily learn）、比较级结构（more readily than）

questions.stem: 第 33 空
questions.expl: ) specific 详解：语法判断：空格前为介词“to”，后为“frequencies”，需填形容词修饰名词。语义判断：前文提到年轻大脑根据常听声音自我连接，此处指“分配给特定频率”，“specific”（特定的）符合语境。 涉及知识点：形容词修饰名词（specific frequencies）、语义逻辑（大脑区域与频率的对应关系）

questions.stem: 第 34 空
questions.expl: 详解：语法判断：空格前为“the”，后为“of space”，需填名词。语义判断：前文提到“assigning areas”（分配区域），此处指“空间分布”，“distribution”（分布）符合语境，指黑暗环境改变频率的空间分布。 涉及知识点：名词作宾语（distribution of space）、同义呼应（assigning areas 与 distribution 语义关联）

questions.stem: 第 35 空
questions.expl: ) speculate 详解：语法判断：主语“We”，后为that宾语从句，需填动词原形作谓语。语义判断：前文提到“不知道这些模式的原因”，此处指“推测”可能与老鼠的注意力有关，“speculate”（推测、猜测）符合语境。 涉及知识点：动词原形（一般现在时）、语义逻辑（未知原因与推测的关系）

questions.stem: 36. Judging from the slowing rate of sales growth,there is still hope to combat bottled water.
questions.expl: 题干关键词“slowing rate of sales growth”“hope”，定位到E段。E段提到“瓶装水销售增长速度已开始放缓（今年增长7%，去年8%），希望并非遥不可及”，题干是对该段内容的概括，“slowing rate of sales growth”对应“the rate of growth has begun to ease”，“there is still hope”对应“hope is not entirely out of reach”。 涉及知识点：段落主旨概括、同义替换（ease 对应 slowing）

questions.stem: 37. Bottled water manufacturers base their arguments against bans of plastic bottles on health concerns rather than on profits.
questions.expl: 题干关键词“Bottled water manufacturers”“against bans”“health concerns rather than profits”，定位到H段。H段指出“瓶装水生产商反对禁令，担忧的是健康问题而非利润”，题干与原文同义，“Bottled water manufacturers”对应“water bottlers”，“against bans”对应“don't support bans”，“base their arguments on health concerns”对应“raise concerns about health rather than profit margins”。 涉及知识点：人物观点定位、同义替换（profit margins 对应 profits）

questions.stem: 38. Sales of bottled water in Britain hit a record high last year even though people are increasingly aware that plastics are environmentally unfriendly.
questions.expl: 题干关键词“Sales of bottled water in Britain”“a record high”“environmentally unfriendly”，定位到B段。B段提到“瓶装水市场活跃，尽管人们意识到塑料的环境危害，但去年英国瓶装水销售额达5.584亿英镑，创纪录”，题干是对该段的概括，“hit a record high”对应“worth a record £558.4 million”，“increasingly aware that plastics are environmentally unfriendly”对应“increasing awareness of the harm plastics do”。 涉及知识点：事实细节与转折关系（despite 引导的让步关系）、同义替换（Britain 对应 UK）

questions.stem: 39. It often happens that people can lack reason when faced with skillful marketing.
questions.expl: 题干关键词“It often happens”“lack reason”“skillful marketing”，定位到L段。L段第一句“clever marketing can beat reason”（巧妙的营销策略能战胜理性）与题干“人们面对巧妙营销时往往失去理智”同义，“As is so often the case”对应“It often happens”。 涉及知识点：主旨句定位、同义替换（clever marketing 对应 skillful marketing；beat reason 对应 lack reason）

questions.stem: 40. One city on the west coast ofAmerica has banned single-use bottles from its property and events.
questions.expl: 题干关键词“One city on the west coast of America”“banned single-use bottles”“property and events”，定位到G段。G段提到“旧金山已禁止在城市公有财产处所和活动中使用一次性塑料瓶”，旧金山是美国西海岸城市，题干与原文同义，“banned single-use bottles from its property and events”对应“has banned them from city property and events”（them 指代 single-use bottles）。 涉及知识点：地理常识（旧金山位于美国西海岸）、指代关系识别（them 对应 single-use bottles）

questions.stem: 41. Manufacturing and shipping ofplastic water bottles consume a tremendous amount offossil fuels.
questions.expl: 题干关键词“Manufacturing and shipping”“plastic water bottles”“fossil fuels”，定位到C段。C段提到“制造和运输塑料水瓶需要耗费大量的化石燃料”，题干与原文同义，“Manufacturing and shipping”对应“make and ship”，“a tremendous amount of”对应“oceans of”。 涉及知识点：同义替换（make and ship 对应 manufacturing and shipping；oceans of 对应 a tremendous amount of）

questions.stem: 42. One large beverage company has adapted its operations when confronted with challenges from health and environmental advocates.
questions.expl: 题干关键词“One large beverage company”“challenges from health and environmental advocates”“adapted its operations”，定位到K段。K段介绍百事公司（大型饮料公司）面临健康和环境挑战时的调整：收购SodaStream、推出可重复使用水瓶和风味包，题干是对该段内容的概括，“adapted its operations”对应原文中的具体举措。 涉及知识点：段落主旨概括、企业行为与挑战的对应关系

questions.stem: 43. Bottled water is considerably more expensive than tap water.
questions.expl: 题干关键词“Bottled water”“tap water”“more expensive”，定位到A段。A段对比了自来水（一升不到半便士）和瓶装水（一升远超1英镑）的价格，明确瓶装水价格远高于自来水，题干是对该对比的结论提炼。 涉及知识点：价格对比与结论提炼、常识换算（1英镑=100便士）

questions.stem: 44. Fountains could be seen in cities before bottled water became popular
questions.expl: 题干关键词“Fountains”“cities”“before bottled water became popular”，定位到I段。I段提到“在塑料和市场营销让人们认为需要瓶装水之前，饮水器是城市的固定设施”，题干与原文同义，“could be seen in cities”对应“were an urban fixture”，“bottled water became popular”对应“people think they needed bottled water”。 涉及知识点：时间对比（before 引导的时间状语）、同义替换（urban fixture 对应 could be seen in cities）

questions.stem: 45. More people have taken to bottled water because of their health awareness.
questions.expl: 题干关键词“More people”“have taken to bottled water”“health awareness”，定位到F段。F段提到“健康意识增加了瓶装水的受欢迎程度，更多人选择瓶装水”，题干与原文同义，“have taken to bottled water”对应“are taking it up”（it 指代 bottled water），“because of their health awareness”对应“health awareness has boosted its desirability”。 涉及知识点：同义替换（take to 对应 take up；boost desirability 对应 make more popular）

questions.stem: 46. What has the author come to realise since entering university?

options.A: He needs a crash course on financial terms.
options.B: He is very much lacking in financial literacy.
options.C: It requires consistent education to be financially independent.
options.D: It is unrealistic to give all Australian youth a financial education.

questions.expl: 定位到第一段第一句“作为一名大学生，我逐渐意识到自己对金钱的了解有多么匮乏”。选项B“非常缺乏金融知识”与原文“how little I know about money”同义；选项A是作者的行动而非意识到的内容；选项C未提及“财务独立”；选项D与原文“澳大利亚年轻人应接受金融教育”的隐含态度矛盾。 涉及知识点：细节定位（段首主旨句）、同义替换（lacking in financial literacy 对应 how little I know about money）

questions.stem: 47. How did the author feel in today's money world?

options.A: Badly equipped to survive.
options.B: Ignorant of financial literature.
options.C: Barely capable ofmoving ahead.
options.D: Overwhelmed by the resources online.

questions.expl: 定位到第四段最后一句“我觉得自己是在没有技能和救生衣的情况下在金融海洋中航行”，比喻作者在金融世界中缺乏应对能力，即“生存能力很差”。选项B“对金融文献一无所知”未提及；选项C“勉强能够前进”无对应；选项D“被网上资源淹没”与原文“有很多优秀资源”不符。 涉及知识点：比喻修辞理解（sailing the financial seas with no skills and no life jacket）、语义推断

questions.stem: 48. What did the author realise after talking to his friends?

options.A: They were as keen as he was on financial matters.
options.B: The schooling system was to blame for his trouble.
options.C: High schoolers knew nothing about the modern financial world.
options.D: Financial courses were as unpopular as compulsory English classes.

questions.expl: 定位到第五段“不是我无知，而是学校教育体系中缺乏金融教育，才让高中生在现代金钱世界中严重落伍”，即作者的困境源于教育体系。选项A未提及“朋友们热衷于金融事务”；选项C“一无所知”过于绝对，原文是“严重落伍”；选项D未对比金融课程与英语课的受欢迎程度。 涉及知识点：因果关系定位（not...but... 强调原因）、语义限定（avoid overstatement）

questions.stem: 49. What is the author's idea of a financial education course?

options.A: It should foresee students'needs after graduation.
options.B: It should provide students with some basic knowledge.
options.C: It should be taught the same way as English is taught.
options.D: It should be integrated into high school education.

questions.expl: 定位到第七段“金融教育课程不应该只是为期一天的活动，而应该是贯穿整个高中的一门课程”，即应纳入高中教育。选项A“预见毕业后需求”未提及；选项B“提供基础知识”是课程的一部分，非核心观点；选项C错误，作者对比英语课是强调“贯穿高中”的设置形式，而非教学方式。 涉及知识点：段落主旨提炼、对比论证的核心目的（英语课与金融课的对比）

questions.stem: 50. What would financial literacy do to young people?

options.A: Allow them to enter adulthood with financial security.
options.B: Enable them to look after themselves without worrying about money.
options.C: Render them confident and secure in terms ofmoney management.
options.D: Help them become familiar with the world ofmoney.

questions.expl: 定位到最后一段“让年轻人熟悉金钱世界，使他们充满自信和安全感，能够管理好自己的钱财”，即金融知识让年轻人在理财方面有信心和安全感。选项A“经济保障”未提及；选项B“不用为金钱担心”过于绝对；选项D是目的而非作用。 涉及知识点：细节定位（段尾结论句）、语义区分（目的与作用的差异）

questions.stem: 51. What do people believe chocolates can do?

options.A: Cheer them up instantly.
options.B: Create happy calories.
options.C: Conceal emotional distress.
options.D: Relieve them of heart trouble.

questions.expl: 定位到第一段第三句“我们都相信巧克力能让我们瞬间快乐”，即“让他们立刻开心起来”。选项B错误，原文是“输送快乐的卡路里”而非“制造”；选项C“掩饰情绪痛苦”错误，原文是“摆脱”；选项D“缓解心脏问题”未提及。 涉及知识点：细节定位、同义替换（cheer them up instantly 对应 delight us in an instant）

questions.stem: 52. What was scientists'recent assertion about chocolates?

options.A: They could become a rare treat in the near future.
options.B: They could calm people down a bit in times of crisis.
options.C: They could prevent people from getting heartbroken.
options.D: They could become unavailable in less than 30 years.

questions.expl: 定位到第二段第一句“科学家们声称巧克力可能在2050年之前不复存在”，2050年距离题干提问时（2024年）不到30年，即“可能在不到30年的时间里消失”。选项A“稀有食品”未提及；选项B、C是巧克力的作用，非科学家的断言。 涉及知识点：数字计算（2050-2024<30）、主旨句定位（科学家断言的核心内容）

questions.stem: 53. What would happen ifthe cacao farms were shifted to cooler mountainous areas?

options.A: The natural habitat ofwildlife there would be ruined.
options.B: The cacao farmers would have a tough time to adapt.
options.C: The rainforests would be shrinking dramatically.
options.D: The quality of cocoa beans would suffer greatly.

questions.expl: 定位到第三段第三句“这些农场将不得不转移到凉爽的山区，那里是野生动物的自然栖息地”，暗示此举会破坏野生动物栖息地。选项B“种植者难以适应”、C“热带雨林缩小”、D“可可豆质量下降”均未提及。 涉及知识点：语义推断（栖息地与农场种植的冲突）、细节定位

questions.stem: 54. What do we learn about the cacao farms in the crisis ofglobal warming?

options.A: They try to seek help from gene-editing scientists.
options.B: They decide to move to cooler mountainous areas.
options.C: They have suffered a lot due to a decrease in produce.
options.D: They have benefited by raising prices of cocoa beans.

questions.expl: 定位到第四段“全球变暖的危机已经对可可农场的产量产生了严重的负面影响，导致巧克力价格飞涨”，即产量减少使农场遭受损失。选项A“寻求基因编辑帮助”是科学家的行为，非农场；选项B“决定搬到山区”是推测，非已发生的事实；选项D“通过提价受益”未提及，价格飞涨是结果而非农场的受益行为。 涉及知识点：因果关系定位（全球变暖→产量下降→价格上涨）、主体区分（农场与科学家的不同行为）

questions.stem: 55. What are scientists trying to do in the University ofCalifornia's new bio-sciences building?

options.A: Build rows ofrefrigerated greenhouses for research on cacao seedlings
options.B: Gene-edit cacao seedlings for them to withstand a drier,warmer climate.
options.C: Produce chocolates with the latest gene-editing technology.
options.D: Transplant the genes oftougher plants to cacao seedlings.

questions.expl: 定位到最后一段“科学家们将对幼苗的DNA进行微小、精确的改变，以使可可作物在更温暖、更干燥的气候条件下存活”，即对可可幼苗进行基因编辑，使其适应干燥温暖的气候。选项A“建造冷藏温室”是实验设施，非核心目的；选项C“生产巧克力”未提及；选项D“移植其他植物基因”错误，原文是“修改自身DNA”。 涉及知识点：细节定位（实验目的）、同义替换（withstand a drier, warmer climate 对应 survive in warmer and drier climates）
